confidence_rationale: Nature paper; names detachment/derailment as WHY novelty bonuses plateau and shows an archive+return mechanism clears a floor->competent gap novelty cannot (>43k vs ~11k RND on Montezuma). Directly on-point for the class-choice; buildable in a small gridworld.
failure_signatures: Detachment: novelty/intrinsic-reward algorithms forget how to reach previously visited promising states once the local bonus is consumed, so the bonus stops pulling the agent back to the true frontier.
Derailment: stochastic exploratory actions prevent reliable RETURN to a known good state to explore onward from it.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Novelty/intrinsic-motivation exploration fails via detachment and derailment; an archive of visited states plus a deterministic return-then-explore loop fixes both, scoring >43,000 mean on Montezuma's Revenge (vs RND ~11,000) and solving all previously-unsolved Atari games.
mapping.ree_translation: The archive+return mechanism is the concrete 'different class' REE's open question hunts for: it decouples reaching a frontier state from exploring at it (which novelty bonuses conflate), and directly explains why REE's RND arm stalled at 5.22.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Full Go-Explore assumes a resettable/deterministic env and a state-cell archive; both are cheap in a small gridworld (cell = discretised z_world, return = replay/reset), but the Atari competence numbers do not transfer verbatim to the forage metric.
mapping.source_context: Deep RL on hard-exploration Atari (Montezuma's Revenge, Pitfall), with save/restore or goal-conditioned return.

confidence_components.notes: Nature venue; the RND-vs-Go-Explore gap on the SAME benchmark is the load-bearing datapoint that the missing ingredient is memory+return, not a stronger bonus.
